narr: A fairly moist and unstable environment ahead of a shortwave trough allowed for showers and thunderstorms to begin forming across central Pennsylvania during the morning hours of July 14, 2025. Showers and thunderstorms became more numerous into the early afternoon hours, pushing eastward through the evening hours. Saturated soils across eastern Pennsylvania from recent flooding allowed for numerous instances of flash flooding, including numerous water rescues in York, Lancaster, and Lycoming counties. In particular, Rapho Township (York County) observed multiple flooded roadways, water rescues, and flooding impacting homes and businesses during the evening hours. Thunderstorms also produced a couple instances of wind damage in northern York County.

East Canal Road flooded in Dover.
A water rescue took place approximately 2 miles west-southwest of East Prospect when a pickup truck was washed off of the roadway.

A water rescue was reported approximately 2 miles southeast of Hallam. Water rose as high as the grill of the car.

Heavy rain caused a closure of State Route 441 south of Columbia Borough and into Washington Township with public reports of swift moving water in the vicinity. The roadway remained damaged from the flash flooding and remained closed through the afternoon hours of July 15, 2025.

PennDOT responded to a mudslide along US Route 220 near Picture Rocks.

Flash flooding led to a water rescue on Fairview Street in Mount Joy. Two people were extracted from a vehicle.

A vehicle became stuck on a flooded roadway at Green Park Drive in Mount Joy, resulting in a water rescue.

Flash flooding led to the closure of both the eastbound and westbound lanes of US-30 between Mountville and Columbia. All lanes reopened at 6 pm.

A water rescue was reported approximately 1 mile southwest of Mountville, where a vehicle got stuck in fast moving water with two occupants.
